title: Existence of a counit-normalized trace on one dualizing quotient system
statement:
theorem integralDualizingSystemTraceData_exists
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X)
    (G : CoefPairingSystem l E (finiteDualizingCompactification D X) S)
    (Q : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E X) ℤ)
    (eQ : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E X n).obj (coefTraceInput l E X Q) ≅
        integralDualizingFiniteTerm l E D X n)
    (hQ : ∀ {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m),
      (coefficientSequenceDerivedTransition l E X h).app (coefTraceInput l E X Q) ≫
          (normalizedDVRRes l E X h).map (eQ n).hom =
        (eQ m).hom ≫
          (Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (normalizedDVRRes l E X h)).homEquiv _ _
            (integralDualizingFiniteComparison l E D X hl h)) :
    Nonempty (IntegralDualizingSystemTraceData D l E X S G Q eQ)

source.place: Second proof paragraph: finite mapping-complex comparisons and reduction-compatible counits.

proof.text: Apply the finite counit compatibility theorem to obtain c and eU and adjacent compatibility of the explicitly prescribed finite trace words.

Apply varying-ring derived evaluation fullness on the base scheme to the support object and the tensor unit, using the prescribed finite trace words and the compatibility just proved. Obtain a system morphism t with exactly these evaluations.

Set supportComparison=c, unitEvaluation=eU and trace=t. For trace_evaluation rewrite by the lifting evaluation equation, expand the finite trace word, reassociate, and cancel (eU n).inv followed by (eU n).hom. This is the original required word.

proof_origin.place: Second proof paragraph: separate finite quotient counit compatibility from the generic lifting of compatible derived evaluation maps, then cancel the finite unit comparison.
